facts.state_of_play:
At a Senate hearing Wednesday, Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment 111 times. Republican Sen. Rand Paul led the hearing and said there is a "very real chance" Fauci could be prosecuted. A Senate committee plans a contempt vote next week. Fauci's private notes were also a subject of scrutiny. Legal experts called the Fifth Amendment strategy sound but politically damaging, and the Biden pardon may be tested. Trump said he watched the entire 3-hour-plus hearing.

Todd Blanche has since been sworn in as Attorney General. Hours after his swearing-in, the DOJ Office of Legal Counsel published a memo — signed by AAG T. Elliot Gaiser — arguing that executive privilege can extend to Trump's communications with private advisers, provided those communications are confidential and related to presidential decision-making. The memo would shield those advisers from congressional and legal investigations. The New Republic frames this as Blanche immediately breaking promises made to GOP senators Cornyn and Tillis, who had conditioned their support on written assurances about the Trump-IRS settlement and related matters.

contradictions.text: Ledger held Blanche's nomination was in jeopardy pending promises to Cornyn/Tillis; item asserts Blanche was sworn in and immediately acted contrary to those commitments.

facts.state_of_play: Iran launched ballistic missiles in an attempted surprise attack on US military installations in the Middle East; the US says it thwarted the attack. Trump threatened severe retaliation. A drone struck a US-owned gas storage tanker at Egypt's Damietta port. Oil prices surged 7% above $90/barrel. US oil inventories are at precariously low levels. Internally, Trump is exasperated as top officials cannot agree on an Iran strategy. It has also emerged that during last month's NATO summit in Turkey, the White House carried out an elaborate ruse to protect Trump from a credible Iranian assassination threat — now reported to have included multiple intelligence streams, among them a threat involving a shoulder-fired missile, with Iran known to have had details of Trump's hotel stay. Trump was hidden in an airport catering container and moved to a military C-32A jet for a secret flight out of Turkey. Senior officials including Secretary of State Rubio, Treasury Secretary Bessent, and deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, along with Communications Director Steven Cheung and members of the press corps, were left aboard Air Force One as unwitting decoys; the decoy plane was escorted by US fighter jets to the United Kingdom. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Chief of Staff Dan Scavino, Oval Office operations director Walt Nauta, and personal assistant Natalie Harp flew with Trump on the secret plane. Trump publicly confirmed the switch on Tuesday, saying the Secret Service and military advised it — but also made the contradictory claim that the jet he secretly boarded was at 'greater risk' than the decoy Air Force One. White House journalists are outraged that the threat was never relayed to them. Trump's biographer Michael Wolff has theorized that Trump himself leaked the story to the Washington Post. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer has personally demanded a full congressional briefing on the operation; Democrats broadly have called for such a briefing. Katie Miller publicly attacked Washington Post reporter Dan Lamothe, who broke the story. The Federal Reserve, chaired by Kevin Warsh, voted 9-3 to hold interest rates steady for the fifth consecutive time, keeping the federal funds rate at 3.5%–3.75%; three members dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike, the first three-dissent vote in a decade. US borrowing costs are at a 19-year high. The Dow closed down over 1,000 points on the news. The hold is seen as a win for Trump, though it contrasts with Warsh's own hawkish rhetoric. F1 is weighing moving its season-closing Middle East races to Europe, with a mid-September decision deadline. Separately, Trump announced a $22.5 billion redesign of Dulles International Airport. In football governance, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has announced a plan to create a new subsidiary to run part of the World Cup and sell a 20% stake to private investors in a venture valued at $20bn, with Joshua Kushner named as the investor; federations have until September 19 to decide. The plan has triggered furious backlash: UEFA called an emergency meeting of its 55 members to coordinate a response, with a European boycott of FIFA tournaments including the Women's World Cup under consideration. UEFA, Concacaf, and the Asian Football Confederation are now jointly developing an alternative governance framework for world football, going beyond boycott threats to propose a replacement system. Calls for Infantino's resignation have reached a fever pitch. Trump has intervened publicly on Truth Social to defend Infantino. During the World Cup, US federal authorities seized 44 drones and $9 million in fake FIFA merchandise in Houston.

facts.state_of_play: Explosions reported in Kyiv after Zelenskyy warned of a Russian massive attack planned over several days; Russia has now struck Ukrainian cities with missiles, drones, and glide bombs, killing at least 10 civilians. North Korean ballistic missiles were used in strikes on Zaporizhzhia, killing seven civilian workers at the Metinvest steel plant and injuring 21; three more civilians including a 15-year-old boy were killed by Russian drones and artillery. Zelenskyy also warns Putin will use the Russian election — in which opposition to the war is banned — as a pretext for a major troop call-up. Russia's Supreme Court has now banned the country's only anti-war party from next month's parliamentary elections, the latest move to silence dissent. Ukraine is also targeting Wildberries, a Russian retail giant akin to Amazon, as part of an effort to bring the sense of war home to the Russian population. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) warns that Putin is preparing to use this winter to break Kyiv, and will not enter serious negotiations if he believes he has a viable military path. Separately, Putin has ordered a probe following the humiliation of Russia's Navy Day parade. Russia has released former US Marine Robert Gilman, 32, after more than four years in prison; Putin granted a humanitarian pardon and Trump is credited with securing the release. The State Department stated explicitly that no prisoner exchange took place and Washington made no concessions. Fox News had framed the release as a prisoner exchange, which the US government has now denied. Gilman had been in a dissociative stupor for 47 days and was gravely ill; his father disputes the Russian account of his arrest. Trump has signed an executive order overhauling the childhood vaccine schedule, drawing pushback from doctors, pharma, and public health experts. A 7.4-magnitude earthquake — Colombia's strongest on record — has struck western Colombia, killing at least 240 people and leaving more than 3,000 missing; rescuers are racing to find survivors amid fears the death toll will rise steeply. A 32-year-old woman was pulled alive from a collapsed apartment on Tuesday, and footage circulating on social media shows a baby being rescued from the rubble of a destroyed building in Cali. The Trump administration has pledged $15.5 million in relief.

facts.state_of_play: A Fox News poll shows Roy Cooper leading Michael Whatley by 9 points in the North Carolina Senate race, with Democrats holding an enthusiasm edge over Republicans. Democratic Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs has selected former Republican Mayor John Giles, now independent, as her running mate. In Minnesota, progressive Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan won the Democratic Senate primary by 20 points over moderate Rep. Angie Craig, in a race defined by anti-ICE anger following the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. Flanagan, backed by Bernie Sanders and Ilhan Omar, could become the first Native woman in the Senate. Her win is the latest in a series of progressive victories over moderates in the Midwest — including Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan U.S. Senate primary win the prior week — and marks a second straight primary setback for Democratic Senate Leader Chuck Schumer. Flanagan faces baggage from a Minnesota fraud scandal that occurred during her tenure as Lt. Gov. Former TV sports reporter Michele Tafoya won the Republican Senate primary in Minnesota and will face Flanagan in November. Minnesota is the first state to set all-female matchups in both its biggest races: Flanagan vs. Tafoya for Senate, and Klobuchar vs. Demuth for governor. Ilhan Omar has been projected to win the Democratic primary in Minnesota's 5th Congressional District. Sen. Amy Klobuchar has been projected to win the Minnesota DFL gubernatorial primary and will face Minnesota House Speaker Lisa Demuth in November; Demuth defeated Trump-backed MyPillow founder Mike Lindell, who received roughly 31% of the vote, losing by about 11 points (over 45,000 votes). Lindell has requested a recount and says he will pay nearly $1 million for the hand recount, since Minnesota only funds automatic recounts when the margin is under 0.25%. In Minnesota's 1st Congressional District, GOP incumbent Brad Finstad survived a primary against challengers Gregory Goetzman and Oliver Morlan. In Connecticut, former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin has been projected to defeat veteran Democratic incumbent Rep. John Larson in the House primary. Larson's loss makes him the 10th House incumbent to lose a primary this cycle, an unusually high figure driven by Democrats pushing leaders to pass the torch to a younger, more progressive generation and Republicans reckoning with Trump's influence. In Wisconsin, Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley defeated democratic socialist Francesca Hong in a stunningly narrow Democratic gubernatorial primary — winning by less than a percentage point — after re-entering the race and securing an endorsement from outgoing Gov. Tony Evers, who called Crowley 'the future of the party.' Crowley, who could become the state's first Black governor, will face Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany in November. Following her loss, Hong endorsed Crowley. Sabato's Crystal Ball subsequently shifted the Wisconsin governor's race toward Democrats. In South Carolina's special GOP Senate primary, Darline Graham (32.6%) and Rep. Ralph Norman (24%) have advanced to an Aug. 25 runoff, with Rep. Russell Fry finishing third at 20.3%. Trump-backed Graham denied being a 'nepo senator.' Ahead of the runoff, Graham and Norman debated at the Newberry Opera House on Aug. 18, 2026, where Graham admitted 'national security is not my thing' and, per fuller reporting, said 'I'm just going to be honest here... not that informed on national security, so - but I do support the military,' drawing gasps and boos from the crowd, while Norman blasted Senate GOP leaders' five-week recess as 'a slap in the face' amid the stalled SAVE Act. The debate flub sparked widespread criticism, including from MAGA podcaster Megyn Kelly, who called Graham's answer 'disqualifying,' and prompted President Trump to schedule an Aug. 21 campaign rally for Graham in Myrtle Beach ahead of the runoff. Trump's endorsements have broadly flopped in major statewide governor races: in addition to Lindell, Trump-backed Andy Ogles (TN) and Amir Hassan (MI) also lost their primaries; Hassan lost to Thomas Smith. An analysis by G. Elliott Morris found that primary election polls miss by an average of 13 points, and prediction markets were also shown to have failed on the Hong result in Wisconsin. El-Sayed's historic nomination as the first Muslim nominated by a major party for U.S. Senate has triggered anti-Muslim vitriol on multiple fronts, tempering elation among Muslim Americans. El-Sayed also faces a significant fundraising challenge in the general election, with Sanders expected to need to provide more active support to shepherd him through November.

facts.state_of_play: NYC Council is investigating four prediction markets (Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Gemini Titan) for deceptive marketing and targeting minors. Separately, the Trump administration declared a market emergency and ordered Kalshi to keep operating despite a New York state lawsuit, creating a federal-state clash. NYC Mayor Mamdani's $70M city-run grocery proposal faces industry opposition, and his broader political honeymoon is ending amid a troubled pied-a-terre tax rollout. AT&T disclosed it uses 45B AI tokens/day and aims to shift 70-80% of AI usage to open models. Trump and two aides have been sued in federal court in Manhattan by The Intercept and Freedom of the Press Foundation over a Trump Media subscription service charging up to $100,000/month for faster access to Truth Social posts; plaintiffs allege the scheme is corrupt and unconstitutional. Trump Media has signed up more than 10 customers. Trump has also signed proclamations imposing new drone tariffs and ordered the Navy to allow shipbuilding abroad. The USS Abraham Lincoln mental health and conditions crisis has escalated further: the wife of a sailor who went overboard last month is speaking out publicly, sharing texts in which the sailor told her he had raised mental health concerns with leadership but was brushed off. The father of another sailor has also spoken out about conditions and deployment length. Family members, including one who told MS NOW that a sailor was eating only half a cup of rice and two tortillas per day, are directly blaming the president and government for the crisis. Senate Democrats, including Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, have specifically demanded answers from the Navy about conditions and the record-length deployment. Blumenthal noted the Lincoln has been deployed for 250 days and has not come ashore in over 200 days, a record. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, speaking from Panama, dismissed reports of deteriorating conditions as 'completely misrepresented.' The Lincoln has now spent 260 uninterrupted days at sea supporting the U.S.-Iran war, with sailors and families reporting food shortages including no milk for three months and rotten meat, broken plumbing, and multiple personnel attempting to jump overboard. The USS George Washington, which departed Vietnam last week, is now en route to replace the Lincoln in the Middle East. A Navy official previously denied any observed increase in suicidal ideations or attempts. The crisis has now spread to a second carrier: loved ones of sailors aboard the USS George H.W. Bush, at sea for 146 days, report it has virtually no food, water, or soap, with low morale and no end in sight. Separately, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the U.S. will pursue unprecedented economic isolation of Iran combined with a continued blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. has now stated the naval blockade of Iranian ports could continue indefinitely, and two more ships have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, bringing transit there to a near standstill. U.S. and Iranian officials are sending contrasting messages about who controls the strait, with experts describing the situation as a deadlock.

facts.state_of_play: Summer 2026 is on course to be the UK's hottest on record, surpassing a record set in 2025. The Met Office has issued only its second-ever extreme heat warning, now extended, with temperatures hitting 38.1C. All of England is under amber heat health alert. Over 10,000 homes are without water, reservoirs are drying up, a ghost village has emerged, wildfires are burning homes, and last month's wildfire tally broke records. In Stourbridge, West Midlands, wildfires have hospitalised three firefighters and a child, with PM Andy Burnham saying he is in touch with local leaders including West Midlands Mayor Richard Parker. Twenty wildfires are now raging across south Wales, with 200 soldiers deployed to reinforce exhausted firefighters as fire chiefs call the situation 'exceptional'; Burnham has called Britain a 'tinderbox' and imposed a temporary ban on disposable barbecues. London bus drivers have gone on strike amid the extreme heat. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has chaired an emergency Cobra committee meeting in response. Separately, Ofwat has provisionally approved 13 water companies to raise customer bills to fund £3.4bn of investment by 2030, with Southern Water customers facing the steepest rise of £80 per year. A passenger train carrying 150 passengers has derailed near Lewes in East Sussex on what was the UK's fifth hottest day ever, injuring at least 18 people, two seriously; rails are believed to have buckled in the extreme heat. Experts warn Britain's railways are woefully behind in adapting to extreme weather. Southern Railway cancelled services until 10pm. British Transport Police, air ambulance, and rail crash investigators attended the scene. Wildfires are spreading across Europe, with 500 people evacuated in southwest France, hundreds of arson suspects arrested in France, and a Croatian holiday resort fire killing one person, injuring 40 and forcing 1,200 evacuations; blazes also hit Germany, Greece and Spain. Two people have died in wildfires on the Greek island of Salamis, with around 200 firefighters battling two blazes there. Belgium is fighting its biggest forest fire in more than a century near the German border, with 600 people evacuated and helicopters deployed. Across Europe more broadly, another day of near-record heat struck on Friday, though temperatures are expected to retreat to seasonal averages in the coming days.

Hospitals in Cali sustained damage, forcing medical staff to prioritize critical patients. Civilian databases still estimate ~4,000 missing versus the official figure of ~400. Conspiracy theories falsely blaming an Alaska research program for the earthquake have spread on social media. Colombia is now grappling with the rebuilding phase; the Chocó region, predominantly Afro-Colombian and Indigenous, faces deepening hunger and homelessness according to its governor, while Colombian superstar Shakira visited affected areas and pledged to help build at least 10 new schools.

facts.state_of_play: Nigel Farage has won the Clacton by-election with 62.8% of the vote and 22,239 votes, surpassing his previous Clacton total of 21,225 — though turnout was roughly 10,000 lower than at the general election two years ago. Farage explicitly triggered the by-election in protest at parliamentary and media scrutiny of his finances. Count Binface — the alter ego of comedian Jon Harvey — finished second with 9,455 votes (over a quarter of the vote) and declared himself 'the winning candidate who bothered to turn up'; he has since announced he will perform at the Edinburgh Fringe. Farage claimed victory before the official announcement, skipped the count citing a credible threat, and cancelled a major speech planned for the morning after his win. Mainstream parties shunned the contest as a stunt. The electoral watchdog has reopened its investigation into a £5 million donation from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne following Farage's win. If the standards probe goes against Farage, a second Clacton by-election could be triggered. Only two of the 34 candidates secured enough votes to reclaim their deposits; one candidate received just seven votes.

facts.state_of_play: A total solar eclipse — the only one of 2026 and Spain's first in over a century — occurred on Aug. 12, 2026, with a path of totality crossing Greenland, Iceland, and northern Spain (approx. 2 min totality). Tens of millions across western Europe, including the UK and Iceland, witnessed the event, with more than 90% of the Sun covered in the UK and more than 95% in Cornwall. Thousands flocked to viewing spots including Sasamón, Spain; trains were packed and carpools booked. Tourist surges hit small Spanish and European towns, with hotel prices in Spain and Iceland exceeding $1,000/night, though Iceland hotels cut rates closer to the date. On-the-ground reporters included CBS News meteorologist Rob Marciano in Mallorca, France 24's Sarah Morris in Segovia, NBC News's Gadi Schwartz, and eclipse chaser Chris Orion in Sasamón. Scientists also used the eclipse for solar research. Last comparable eclipse visible from European mainland was 1999. Thursday's UK newspaper front pages were dominated by the eclipse.

Vance describes the conflict as entering a 'new phase' centered on economic pressure. facts.state_of_play: A preliminary autopsy on Hayden Panettiere has been released; she was found in cardiac arrest after a 911 call made by boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach, with Narcan present at the scene, and paramedics' resuscitation efforts were unsuccessful. A Greenville police incident report reveals Hickerson and his brother Zach were present at the rented Airbnb where she died, and police found a 'bag of medication' at the scene, which Hickerson reportedly handed over himself. Hickerson had previously pleaded no contest to a domestic violence charge against her. Her estranged mother, Lesley Vogel, has publicly blamed Hickerson for 'enabling' her daughter's death, said Panettiere had 'sadly lost her way,' and in an exclusive NBC interview said she wished her daughter 'had stayed true to herself.' Three days after her death, Greenville police conducted a welfare check at a home in Greenville belonging to Hickerson's grandmother, Betty Ellison, receiving no response. Reports have also alleged a rumored love triangle involving Panettiere and Zach Hickerson. Her death remains under investigation, with no signs of foul play found, and reports of a 'downward swing' preceding her death. She had spoken openly about struggles with addiction, fame, and trauma linked to her Nashville role before her death.

facts.state_of_play: A massive Russian missile and drone barrage struck Kyiv overnight, killing 12-16 people and wounding around 40, hitting a children's hospital, a school, residential blocks and warehouses; Poland activated defensive measures in response, and officials cited Ukraine's ongoing air-defence interceptor shortages. Separately, Ukrainian strikes have knocked out nearly a third of Russia's major oil refineries, prompting fuel shortages and clashes at petrol stations, with Putin's government arresting Russians who complained. This is in addition to the earlier large-scale Ukrainian drone assault on Moscow region and the deadly Russian missile strike on a Kharkiv region village. Additionally, a Russian 'double-tap' drone strike hit a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, Zelensky's hometown, killing 15-16 people and injuring more than 100, with a second wave of drones striking as rescue workers responded. A day later, further Russian strikes killed 6 more Ukrainians, while a Ukrainian drone strike on a home in southern Russia killed two children and injured their parents. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul arrived in Kyiv by special train ahead of Ukraine's 35th independence day as Russia stepped up its attacks.

facts.state_of_play: Indonesia's twin earthquakes (7.7 and 6.4 magnitude) have killed at least 68 people, with thousands still awaiting aid and homeless on Flores Island days after the quake, overshadowing the country's Independence Day. Meanwhile Hurricane Lala weakened to a tropical storm after its eye passed about 30 miles off Hawaii's Big Island without direct landfall, avoiding the first direct hurricane hit on the island in over a century; it still lashed the island with hurricane-force gusts and nearly 3 feet of rain, causing flooding and mudslides, at least one death, more than 100 homes damaged or lost, damage to bridges, and over 180,000 households losing power, per Gov. Josh Green. The storm has since restrengthened into a Category 3 hurricane and moved west, away from Hawaii, where crews are working to restore power and clear roads. Now, just days later, Tropical Storm Moke is poised to hit Hawaii, forecast to bring up to 15 inches of rain and strong winds, with the Big Island again expected to bear the brunt as it passes south late Saturday into Sunday, raising fresh flooding and mudslide concerns in areas already battered by Lala. The storm also struck Maui, stranding tourists, and officials issued a major disaster declaration. Meanwhile the same system fueled the worst Indiana flooding in over 30 years, with the broader Midwest death toll now at least 7, including at least six in Indiana—a 4-year-old boy, two men, and three women—since storms began Aug. 11, per state homeland security spokesperson Liz Woods. Floodwaters peaked along Indianapolis's White River after Mayor Joe Hogsett ordered evacuations and crews conducted water rescues, with rain expected to ease in the capital region on Sunday though the National Weather Service warns flash flooding remains possible across central Indiana. Indiana's governor says the federal government has promised assistance, with more heavy rain expected across Indiana, Illinois and neighboring states this weekend.

facts.state_of_play: Five years after retaking power, the Taliban govern Afghanistan with reports of safer streets but widespread deprivation in jobs and education. Women have been systematically erased from public life via decrees restricting study, work and travel, with UN Women warning over half of women's aid organisations could shut within a year. Individual stories, like that of secretly-teaching doctor Azada, illustrate the toll. Diplomatically, Afghanistan's foreign minister is now urging the US to reopen its embassy and invest, though analysts call this unlikely. Meanwhile, ~70,000 Afghan evacuees in the US on humanitarian parole still lack permanent legal status. Separately, the Taliban detained and then released two UN staff members in Herat.

facts.state_of_play: Three century-old paintings by Renoir, Cézanne, and Matisse were stolen in a 180-second heist from the Magnani-Rocca Foundation near Parma, Italy, valued at €9 million, and have been recovered by Italian police. Separately, eight Matisse works were found at a home in greater São Paulo, Brazil, and one man was arrested. In a separate incident the day after the Parma recovery, four Renaissance paintings by Antonello da Messina, including three panels from his Polittico di San Gregorio, were stolen overnight from the regional museum (MuMe) in Messina, Sicily, during the Ferragosto holiday while 100,000 people attended a religious festival in the city, without triggering any alarms, raising suspicion of a professional operation; Italy's culture minister confirmed the theft and authorities have launched an investigation. Art expert Alberto Fiz estimated the stolen works' value at 70-80 million euros ($81-92 million).

facts.state_of_play: Israeli settlers are escalating a campaign of violence and land expansion across the West Bank: besieging Palestinian homes in villages like Qusra (cutting off food and water), setting fire to a Palestinian home while a mother and her children slept inside, and resettling evacuated sites like Kadim two decades later. On Friday, Israeli settlers and soldiers killed two Palestinians in separate West Bank incidents: 17-year-old Karim Sanad Shalaldeh, shot by settlers, and 58-year-old Fathi Khazem, killed by Israeli forces. Video also emerged of Israeli soldiers themselves throwing belongings out of a besieged Palestinian home in Qusra, alongside settler sieges. Palestinian American homeowner Louai (Loui) Abo Ridi, back from Ohio after 10 days under siege, has directly confronted settlers outside his home despite Israeli military deployment, demanding protection from Israeli forces and the U.S. government. A new Yesh Din report finds settler attacks in Palestinian-administered West Bank areas have almost doubled since 2025 amid a self-proclaimed 'great settlement revolution,' with AJLabs analysis putting the rate at six attacks a day. Separately, settler children attacked a Red Crescent ambulance, the Board of Peace reversed course on a Gaza disarmament deal, Christian families report growing pressure to leave, and Israel opened tenders for over 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement, prompting France, Germany, Britain and Italy to join Europe and Canada in condemning the plan as making Palestinian statehood impossible. An Israeli minister also faces backlash over a gallows site with a 'viewing booth' for hanging Palestinians.

facts.state_of_play: Overnight Russian missile and drone bombardment of Kyiv, involving dozens of missiles, up to 168 drones, and hypersonic weapons, has an escalating confirmed toll, with outlets now reporting between 6 and 17 killed and injuries ranging from 30 to over 40; strikes damaged residential buildings, a children's hospital and a school, and cut power to parts of the capital. Coverage links the assault to Ukraine's Patriot interceptor shortage, with Zelenskyy calling on allies to replenish stockpiles. Ukraine is also seeking Elon Musk's help to deploy Starlink-equipped drones capable of striking Russian missile launchers up to 200km inside Russia. Poland's military activated preventive aviation and defensive measures, and Zelenskyy faces domestic political pressure. A related thread on Russia's strained oil industry has developed further: Ukrainian strikes have knocked out nearly a third of Russia's major refineries, sparking fuel shortages, petrol station fights, and arrests of complaining citizens. This remains separate from other Russia-linked threads: bank withdrawals fearing state seizure; Kanye West's sold-out Russian shows; Russia's UK embassy threatening consequences over British drone use; and Ukrainian drones destroying Wildberries warehouses with Putin's pledge of support.

facts.state_of_play: Hayden Panettiere died at 36 in Greenville, South Carolina, found in cardiac arrest from a suspected overdose at an Airbnb after Brian Hickerson administered Narcan; the DEA has reportedly joined the investigation. New reporting reveals Hickerson was called out in court over alleged drug use just three days before her death, and that Panettiere had traveled to South Carolina with him only a day earlier. A protective order Panettiere filed against Hickerson six years before her death details abuse including hair-pulling and spitting, and further accounts describe multiple prior arrests for his abuse. Zach Hickerson has given a direct account of finding her unconscious and administering Narcan. A neighbor has described Hickerson as 'terrifying,' echoing abuse allegations from her memoir, and texts show him vowing to 'go to war.' Her estranged mother Lesley Vogel has spoken out, and friends including Hilary Duff are sharing tributes. Hickerson's attorney has issued a public statement on his behalf.
